Digital marketing

SEO audits.

Find the changes most likely to improve search performance, with a prioritised list your team can act on.

Discuss this service View brief
Scope of work

What we work on.

Check the technical foundations

A crawl and a Search Console review reveal indexing problems, broken redirects, duplicate pages and slow mobile templates.

Compare content and competitors

We map pages to buyer questions, review backlinks and compare the site with three to five search competitors to find gaps and overlaps.

Get a plan for your team

The audit includes a written report, a walkthrough and fixes ordered by effort and impact. You can implement them internally or discuss follow-on support.

Deliverables

What you receive.

  • Technical, content and link findings backed by examples.
  • A comparison with competing sites and an ordered list of fixes.
  • Written report and a call or recorded walkthrough.
Questions

Before you start.

How much time should we allow?

A typical review takes one to two weeks. A larger site may need longer, so we confirm timing when we agree the scope.

What access does the audit require?

Read access to Analytics and Search Console usually covers the data review. Hosting credentials are unnecessary for the audit.

Can our own developers carry out the work?

Yes. The recommendations are designed for handover, and implementation support can be scoped separately.

Field notes

Further reading.

What is an SEO audit?

An SEO audit examines why important pages struggle to appear in search or attract suitable visitors. Its most useful output is a short, ordered work plan.

Keyword research for beginners

Good keyword research finds the language customers use and matches each useful question to a page that can genuinely answer it.
